To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the frequency of 5-flurorodeoxyuridin (5-FdUR) + caffeine-induced fragile sites is significantly increased in the peripheral blood lymphocytes of patients with malignant melanoma; 2) the expression of fragile sites at 1p22 and 1p32 is significantly enhanced in melanoma patients.

the frequency and distribution of chromosome breaks induced by 5-FdUR plus caffeine in peripheral blood lymphocytes from patients with cutaneous malignant melanoma are significantly higher than those from normal donors.
The total number of 5-FU plus caffeine-induced fragile site expression was significantly higher in patients with melanoma compared to healthy controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for the genetic markers of melanoma.
the possibility of the use of 5-FD plus caffeine-induced fragile site expression as a new cytogenetic marker in the study of human neoplasias.
the possibility of a new approach to the detection of individuals at high risk for the development of malignant melanomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

5-FdUR plus caffeine treatment of lymphocytes from melanoma patients induces more fragile sites, and the expression of several of them, especially those at 1p, is higher in comparison with the control samples.
the fragile site expression in the tumor cells may be a useful marker for the detection of genetic instability in human neoplasias.
1p32, 1p22, and other fragile sites are not only markers of genetic instability but may be involved in the development of malignant tumors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increase in the frequency of chromosome breakage and fragile site expression may be considered as a marker of increased genomic instability, which may be associated with the development and progression of malignant tumors.
the increase in the frequency of fragile sites in PBL of melanoma patients may be considered as an indicator of the genetic instability of these cells.

the increased frequencies and distribution of 1p fragile sites in lymphocyte chromosomes of melanoma patients could be considered as a possible cytogenetic marker for the early detection of this type of tumors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
1p32 is a site of interest in the study of neuroectodermal tumours.
the frequency and distribution of 1p fragile sites are significantly enhanced in PBL from patients with cutaneous malignant melanoma.
fragile sites may be used as biomarkers for cancer risk assessment and early detection of malignant tumors.
